SMTO-LLM-0060 — SMTO couldn't find the model server profile you named

GUID: 5dc03c21-2ac9-577a-b1f7-07ebbf5b54d8
Slug: local-ai-profile-not-found
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • Your request names a model server profile that isn't among the settings this task was given. SMTO won't swap in a different profile, so nothing was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and check there's a parameter made from the Local AI Runtime template with the name your request used. SMTO looks the profile up only by that exact name.
  2. If it's missing, choose Local AI Runtime from the new parameter template list, fill in the Gateway, provider, host and port, and select Save. The profile tells SMTO which computer and program to use for the model server.
  3. Ask SMTO to show the Local AI status for that Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses on that computer, to see whether this model server is already running. This avoids starting a second copy of a model server that's already up.
  4. If it isn't running, send a new message that names the profile with @ (use Copy reference in Parameter Store to get the exact name). A task only gets the profiles named when it starts, so a new message is needed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists your profile when asked for Local AI profiles, and the model server starts.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't create several profiles with the same name; SMTO needs exactly one match.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Local AI profile reference does not resolve to exactly one accepted Parameter binding in the task (missing, duplicated or unreadable), or the Gateway request carried no profile.

What this means

  • The accepted parameter bindings do not resolve exactly one retained profile value, or the Gateway request omits its required profile. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The accepted parameter bindings do not resolve exactly one retained profile value, or the Gateway request omits its required profile.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare profile_ref with the task's accepted parameter bindings and retained revisions; check whether the reference is absent or unresolved.

How to fix it

  • Check the task's accepted parameter_references for the @reference passed to the local_ai tool; create or fix the Local AI Runtime Parameter so exactly one binding matches, then start a new task that names it. Use local_ai.profiles to confirm the accepted reference and revision.
  • Select the correct profile parameter and accept its current revision in a new request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The accepted reference resolves one validated profile on the intended Gateway.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
